scope: Explicit EU5 selectors and area checks for three bounded Pacific validation cases. These proposals do not promote any record into training.

geometry_and_table_manifest.area_method: frozen accepted land-area field with explicit named-island area comparisons

eligibility.reason: Contact-era reconstruction outside 1337 and disputed demographic estimates; no independent saturation fraction.

area_comparison.interpretation: The named EU5 Tahiti row is area-coextensive within 0.37%; no population redistribution or area multiplier is applied.

historical_evidence.pressure_and_uncertainty: Rallu (2024) reconciles early-navigator density observations and post-contact retrodictions, while Sear et al. (2026) tabulates the 198,550 peak reconstruction. The interval is held out because it is post-1337 and demographic rather than an independent capacity measurement.

current_model_diagnostic.comparison: The mechanistic p50 is far below the reconstructed contact population; this is an actionable high-density tropical-island diagnostic, not a training error label.

sources.citation: Sear et al. (2026), Journal of Pacific Archaeology 16(2), Table A1
sources.locator: Table A1, Tahiti row (198,550; 1,045 km2; 190 people/km2).

crosswalks.resolution_method: Direct one-row EU5 selector with frozen area comparison and hash-pinned accepted-table diagnostic.

crosswalks.historical_boundary: Entire Upolu island, Samoa, approximately 1,125 km2.

eligibility.reason: Genetic/demographic reconstruction outside 1337 with unresolved census-versus-effective-population semantics and no independent saturation fraction.

area_comparison.interpretation: The 0.87% area discrepancy is treated as measurement uncertainty; the selector is retained for validation and never rescales the population interval.

historical_evidence.pressure_and_uncertainty: Sear et al. (2026) reports 75,400 for Upolu as part of a 109,000 Samoa genetic reconstruction and cites a separate 70,000 demographic estimate. These are held-out reconstruction values; drought sensitivity and local horticulture provide pressure context but not a saturation label.

current_model_diagnostic.comparison: The model p50 is close to the 70,000-75,400 lower reconstruction but below the 109,000 genetic archipelago total; this is a useful held-out island-density check.

sources.citation: Sear et al. (2026), Journal of Pacific Archaeology 16(2), Table A1
sources.locator: Table A1, Samoa row (109,000 total; 75,400 Upolu; 1,125 km2) and pp. 17-19.
Genetic reconstruction cited by Sear et al.

crosswalks.resolution_method: Direct one-row EU5 selector with conservative area-ratio coverage and frozen accepted-table diagnostic.

crosswalks.historical_boundary: Entire Hawai'i (Big Island), approximately 10,430 km2; four EU5 locations provide a quantified partial selector.

eligibility.reason: Only 81.66% of the published island area is represented; population is reconstructed and agricultural production is model-derived.

area_comparison.interpretation: The partial crosswalk is explicit and remains below the 95% training threshold; no unobserved island population is imputed.

historical_evidence.pressure_and_uncertainty: Ladefoged et al. quantify 572 km2 of feasible intensive agriculture, approximately 97,000 tonnes of potential crop production and 165,000 agricultural workers; archaeological syntheses place a broad fifteenth-century island population peak around 150,000. Neither is treated as an observed carrying-capacity label.

current_model_diagnostic.comparison: The mapped 81.66% footprint already produces a p50 above the reconstructed 100,000-200,000 island interval; because 18.34% of the island is unmapped, this is retained as a qualitative overprediction diagnostic only, never converted into an error label or area-scaled target.

sources.citation: Ladefoged et al. (2009), Journal of Archaeological Science 36:2374-2383
sources.locator: Abstract and pp. 2374-2383: Hawai'i 572 km2 intensive agriculture, 97,000 tonnes and 165,000 workers.

sources.citation: Kirch (2007), Like Shoals of Fish: Archaeology and Population in Pre-Contact Hawai'i

crosswalks.resolution_method: Four explicit named EU5 selectors with calibrated area sum and declared unmapped area; no area or population imputation.

summary.key_result: Tahiti and Upolu provide high-coverage named-island validation checks; Hawai'i Island provides a partial but physically rich intensive-agriculture fixture. All remain out of training.
summary.required_follow_up: Score Tahiti and Upolu in held-out generalization reports, use Hawai'i for physical crop/land diagnostics, and preserve all reconstruction conflicts rather than collapsing them into a target.
